done.why: I ran out of turns while lost in the maze again, trying to find whatever is past the skeleton room. I had 130 points out of 350.

about: It's a cut-down Zork-style treasure hunt under a white house. You go down, kill or bribe a troll, collect treasures (a platinum bar, an ivory torch, a jeweled egg, a painting, a gold coffin with a sceptre) and carry them back to the trophy case. A light-fingered thief roams the maze. Several parts of the old underground are closed off on purpose: the dam is "closed for inspection" and the chasm paths go down into still black water. Weight limits matter, so you keep juggling what you carry.

moments.note: 'go around the house' worked and walked me to the north side.
'tie rope to knife and throw it' refused the tie, then printed 'Thrown.' and quietly threw the rope away in the attic. I had to check my inventory to find out what had gone.
Someone barred the trap door behind me as I went down. Later it opened again with no trouble from above (turn 105).
The troll ate my lunch and then my garlic, and the first sword blow killed him.
Couldn't pick up the platinum bar, 'the sword not least of it'. The world blamed the sword specifically, which I liked even though it was annoying.
Northwest from the canyon doesn't just say 'can't go'. You walk down into flooded black water and step back out with a description. The closed areas felt deliberate.
The dam has a board on it: CLOSED FOR INSPECTION -- The Management. Funny.
Praying at the altar sent me straight up to the forest with everything I was carrying. A great shortcut home.
Left the heavy sword in the bird's nest so I could take the egg. The world let me make the swap.
The chimney allows you, your lamp and one thing more. I put the painting, bottle and manual inside the sack and that counted as one thing. My contrary trick worked.
The painting inside the sack inside the trophy case didn't score until I took it out and put it in the case directly. The case also listed the 'brown sack' as a treasure.
The thief walked through the maze and took my bag of coins before I could get them out.
The maze ate most of my turns. Rooms that look the same, one-way drops, and my landmark (the dropped manual) only got me so far.
Used the altar-prayer shortcut again to carry the gold coffin out, and the score jumped to 130.

wished: Pry the nailed gothic door or the trophy case open with the sword, and get a real answer instead of 'Nice try' or 'isn't one I recognize'
Climb into the coffin, blow out the torch, swim the black water. The world described these well but wouldn't let me try them
Shout after the thief or chase him to get my coins back
Wade further into the flooded passages, or get past the dam
Have more natural phrasings understood ('offer the troll my lunch', 'go upstairs first', 'take everything')
Find the way through the maze to whatever is past the skeleton before my turns ran out

lines.line: The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
lines.why: A dry joke on a door that can't be opened. Set the tone.

lines.line: Only Santa Claus climbs down chimneys.
lines.why: A playful refusal, the kind I was hoping to get by pushing.

lines.line: Whatever is beyond is under it. You step back out of the puddle you were standing in.
lines.why: The best-written moment. A closed-off area that still felt like a place.

lines.line: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.
lines.why: A funny, in-world way of saying 'not here'.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: The weight limit points at what to drop, and that pushed me toward giving the sword to the nest.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear rule I could get around by packing everything into the sack.

lines.line: he quietly abstracted some valuables from your possession, mumbling something about "Doing unto others before..."
lines.why: The thief's entrance. It was annoying and charming at once.

fun.why: Getting around the rules was fun: sword into the nest for the egg (94), everything packed in the sack for the chimney (115-116), praying at the altar as a shortcut home (89, 222). The maze slog (152-198, 233-250) dragged it down.

engagement.why: I kept wanting to get the next treasure home and watch the score climb (103, 124, 230). I lost energy in the maze.

difficulty.why: The troll and the treasures were easy (47-48). The weight limits made me think (56, 114). The maze was hard and took a lot of turns (128-198).

interestingness.why: The closed-off places are written as places, not as walls (62, 64, 69). The weight rule that names the sword and the barred trap door that later reopened kept me guessing.

prose.why: The new lines about water and the dam are evocative and funny (62, 64, 69). The refusals have personality (40, 21). Some of my odd phrasings got only a flat 'That sentence isn't one I recognize' (22, 28, 44).
